name: Order.co
summary: Order.co is a purchasing platform that puts orders from many vendors into one cart and converts requisitions into purchase orders. It publishes no prices and offers a demo instead of a trial. Its trust center lists SOC 2 and ISO 27001, and sign-in works with Okta or Ping Identity.

facts.text: Order.co says buyers can order from many vendors in one cart, and that purchase order creation, fulfillment to vendors and order management are handled in the product.
The FAQ says approval rules can be configured by location, cost center, user role or spend threshold.
Order.co says buyers can use a custom catalog, and that its customer success team handles supplier onboarding and approval-rule setup.
The trust center lists SOC 2 and ISO 27001 and refers to GDPR, without audit dates or scope.
The accounting integrations page names QuickBooks Online, NetSuite and Sage Intacct, and a separate page covers Workday.

plans.name: Order.co
plans.notes: No plans or fees are published. The page offers a demo request

hiddenCosts: The site does not say whether Order.co charges subscription fees, vendor fees or both.
Its savings claim of about 5% on products is a vendor figure we have not verified.
